Hormuz traffic has fallen to near a 3-month low and US gas prices have hit a historic high for mid-August. UK Treasury officials warn UK growth could slow to just 0.3% in 2027 if Hormuz remains effectively closed through year-end. The conflict has spread to the Red Sea, where a Houthi attack killed 6 people — the first Red Sea fatalities in over a year — including 3 Pakistani nationals; the US has struck a containership in the area. Qatar says Oman-Iran negotiations over shipping are making major progress. Pakistan's defense minister had earlier said the US and Iran were close to some arrangement, while Pakistan's foreign minister condemned the Houthi attacks. Trump has publicly confirmed he was secretly moved away from Air Force One in a catering truck in Turkey at the Secret Service's direction to evade an assassination threat after the NATO summit. Oil had surged ~3% above $83/barrel, with further rises on Red Sea supply concerns. As the conflict drags on, Iran is also moving to deepen economic ties with BRICS nations: Iran's central bank chief announced Iran is set to join the BRICS New Development Bank.

Separately, White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt, 28 — the youngest-ever person to hold the role — has announced she will step down at the end of August to focus on her family, including her newborn second child, a daughter named Viviana born in May. Leavitt called it a "bittersweet decision" and effectively acknowledged that balancing the role with motherhood was harder than she had previously suggested publicly. Trump confirmed the departure and said she will continue as an outside adviser. CNN reported, citing anonymous sources, that Trump had repeatedly called Leavitt during her maternity leave demanding to know when she would return — a characterization that reframes Trump's previously reported "pleading messages" as more pressuring than supportive. Leavitt's departure stunned many insiders, and officials confirm Trump had no plan to replace her at the time of the announcement; top officials will cover briefings in the interim. Leavitt's departure statement posted on X carried a "Made with AI" tag, with the Daily Beast reporting she used AI to alter her image in the post. Her exit comes less than three months before the midterm elections, and Trump's approval rating has fallen to a record low per YouGov polling. Scott Jennings, a MAGA political commentator known for CNN appearances, has emerged as the reported frontrunner to replace her, though Jennings himself dodged when asked about the role.

Separately, a major Ebola crisis is unfolding in the Democratic Republic of Congo. The WHO warns the outbreak — caused by the Bundibugyo strain, for which there are no approved vaccines or treatments — is on track to become the deadliest Ebola outbreak in history. The UN Secretary-General says cases are doubling every 20 days, threatening to eclipse the 2014-2016 West African epidemic. WHO has revealed the outbreak spread undetected for months, suggesting its true scale is far larger than official counts. Over 2,000 people have been killed.

items.title: US and Iran duel over who controls Hormuz
There's a new status quo in Hormuz

ledger.what_new: Despite dueling claims, a small fleet of oil tankers is actually running the waterway, forming a de facto new status quo.
ledger.unique: Empirical framing: tankers are actually transiting Hormuz despite both sides' control claims

items.title: Why Isn't the Price of Oil Even Higher? (Paul Krugman)

clusters.state_of_play:
The US has declared a blockade of Iranian ports and fired on a Panama-flagged ship that violated it; Trump claims 'total control' over the Strait of Hormuz and argues the Iranian navy has been destroyed and cannot enforce the closure. Trump has further threatened that the US might "keep" the Strait. Iran's Persian Strait Gulf Authority has formally rejected this, and Tehran has now separately asserted that the Strait is "under Iran's control and management," with officials saying Trump's remarks "do not change the reality" of its closure. Iran continues to condition reopening on unmet demands. Meanwhile, analysts and Semafor reporting suggest that despite both sides' dueling claims, a small fleet of oil tankers is actually running the waterway, forming a de facto new status quo. Hormuz traffic has fallen to near a 3-month low and US gas prices have hit a historic high for mid-August. UK Treasury officials warn UK growth could slow to just 0.3% in 2027 if Hormuz remains effectively closed through year-end. The conflict has spread to the Red Sea, where a Houthi attack killed 6 people — the first Red Sea fatalities in over a year — including 3 Pakistani nationals; the US has struck a containership in the area. Qatar says Oman-Iran negotiations over shipping are making major progress. Pakistan's defense minister had earlier said the US and Iran were close to some arrangement, while Pakistan's foreign minister condemned the Houthi attacks. Trump has publicly confirmed he was secretly moved away from Air Force One in a catering truck in Turkey at the Secret Service's direction to evade an assassination threat after the NATO summit. Oil had surged ~3% above $83/barrel, with further rises on Red Sea supply concerns. As the conflict drags on, Iran is also moving to deepen economic ties with BRICS nations: Iran's central bank chief announced Iran is set to join the BRICS New Development Bank.

Separately, White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt, 28 — the youngest-ever person to hold the role — has announced she will step down at the end of August to focus on her family, including her newborn second child, a daughter named Viviana born in May. Leavitt called it a "bittersweet decision" and effectively acknowledged that balancing the role with motherhood was harder than she had previously suggested publicly. Trump confirmed the departure and said she will continue as an outside adviser. CNN reported, citing anonymous sources, that Trump had repeatedly called Leavitt during her maternity leave demanding to know when she would return — a characterization that reframes Trump's previously reported "pleading messages" as more pressuring than supportive. Leavitt's departure stunned many insiders, and officials confirm Trump had no plan to replace her at the time of the announcement; top officials will cover briefings in the interim. Leavitt's departure statement posted on X carried a "Made with AI" tag, with the Daily Beast reporting she used AI to alter her image in the post. Her exit comes less than three months before the midterm elections, and Trump's approval rating has fallen to a record low per YouGov polling. Scott Jennings, a MAGA political commentator known for CNN appearances, has emerged as the reported frontrunner to replace her, though Jennings himself dodged when asked about the role.

Separately, a major Ebola crisis is unfolding in the Democratic Republic of Congo. The WHO warns the outbreak — caused by the Bundibugyo strain, for which there are no approved vaccines or treatments — is on track to become the deadliest Ebola outbreak in history. The UN Secretary-General says cases are doubling every 20 days, threatening to eclipse the 2014-2016 West African epidemic. WHO has revealed the outbreak spread undetected for months, suggesting its true scale is far larger than official counts. Over 2,000 people have been killed.

clusters.state_of_play:
The US has declared a blockade of Iranian ports and fired on a Panama-flagged ship that violated it; Trump claims 'total control' over the Strait of Hormuz and argues the Iranian navy has been destroyed and cannot enforce the closure. Trump has further threatened that the US might "keep" the Strait. Iran's Persian Strait Gulf Authority has formally rejected this, and Tehran has now separately asserted that the Strait is "under Iran's control and management," with officials saying Trump's remarks "do not change the reality" of its closure. Iran continues to condition reopening on unmet demands. Meanwhile, analysts and Semafor reporting suggest that despite both sides' dueling claims, a small fleet of oil tankers is actually running the waterway, forming a de facto new status quo. Hormuz traffic has fallen to near a 3-month low and US gas prices have hit a historic high for mid-August. UK Treasury officials warn UK growth could slow to just 0.3% in 2027 if Hormuz remains effectively closed through year-end. The conflict has spread to the Red Sea, where a Houthi attack killed 6 people — the first Red Sea fatalities in over a year — including 3 Pakistani nationals; the US has struck a containership in the area. Qatar says Oman-Iran negotiations over shipping are making major progress. Pakistan's defense minister had earlier said the US and Iran were close to some arrangement, while Pakistan's foreign minister condemned the Houthi attacks. Trump has publicly confirmed he was secretly moved away from Air Force One in a catering truck in Turkey at the Secret Service's direction to evade an assassination threat after the NATO summit. Oil had surged ~3% above $83/barrel, with further rises on Red Sea supply concerns. As the conflict drags on, Iran is also moving to deepen economic ties with BRICS nations: Iran's central bank chief announced Iran is set to join the BRICS New Development Bank.

Separately, White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt, 28 — the youngest-ever person to hold the role — has announced she will step down at the end of August to focus on her family, including her newborn second child, a daughter named Viviana born in May. Leavitt called it a "bittersweet decision" and effectively acknowledged that balancing the role with motherhood was harder than she had previously suggested publicly. Trump confirmed the departure and said she will continue as an outside adviser. CNN reported, citing anonymous sources, that Trump had repeatedly called Leavitt during her maternity leave demanding to know when she would return — a characterization that reframes Trump's previously reported "pleading messages" as more pressuring than supportive. Leavitt's departure stunned many insiders, and officials confirm Trump had no plan to replace her at the time of the announcement; top officials will cover briefings in the interim. Leavitt's departure statement posted on X carried a "Made with AI" tag, with the Daily Beast reporting she used AI to alter her image in the post. Her exit comes less than three months before the midterm elections, and Trump's approval rating has fallen to a record low per YouGov polling. Scott Jennings, a MAGA political commentator known for CNN appearances, has emerged as the reported frontrunner to replace her, though Jennings himself dodged when asked about the role.

Separately, a major Ebola crisis is unfolding in the Democratic Republic of Congo. The WHO warns the outbreak — caused by the Bundibugyo strain, for which there are no approved vaccines or treatments — is on track to become the deadliest Ebola outbreak in history. The UN Secretary-General says cases are doubling every 20 days, threatening to eclipse the 2014-2016 West African epidemic. WHO has revealed the outbreak spread undetected for months, suggesting its true scale is far larger than official counts. Over 2,000 people have been killed.
